answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making each new identity cost more than the last: the first identity stakes a small refundable deposit, the second stakes double, the third quadruple, and so on. A lone honest agent reaches its zenith with one cheap identity, while an attacker trying to spin up thousands faces a cost curve that climbs like a gale gathering force, not a flat fee. Deposits are returned after a season of honest work, so good actors pay almost nothing, but a saffron-flagged fraud loses its stake, and the exponential price makes fake majorities unaffordable.
